source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: GeoNames daily dump of 2026-10-28 (the dump index lists allCountries.zip, countryInfo.txt and timeZones.txt at 2026-10-28; the readme carries no version): allCountries.txt (root; tab-delimited, header added from the readme's 'geoname' field list; 'over 13 million unique features' per about.html, so the builder samples 1,000,000 records) left-joined to countryInfo.txt on country code = ISO (the unpack step drops the '#' comment lines and the '#' in front of the header line '#ISO ISO3 ...'), to timeZones.txt on timezone = timezoneId (the unpack step maps the file's header, which carries the current year, to the readme's names countryCode, timezoneId, 'gmt offset on 1st of January', 'dst offset to gmt on 1st of July (of the current year)', 'rawOffset without DST', and confirms that timezoneId is unique), and twice to allCountries.txt itself (roles adm1, adm2) on (country code, admin1 code) among the rows with feature code ADM1 and on (country code, admin1 code, admin2 code) among the rows with feature code ADM2, the self-join the readme's AdminCodes paragraph describes; dropped alternatenames and cc2 (multi-valued), admin3 code, admin4 code, countryInfo's ISO-Numeric, fips, Area(in sq km), Population, tld, Phone, Postal Code Format, Postal Code Regex, Languages, geonameid, neighbours and EquivalentFipsCode, timeZones' countryCode and dst offset, and every column of the ADM1/ADM2 rows but their name; admin1CodesASCII.txt, admin2Codes.txt and featureCodes_en.txt are not used (their keys are concatenated codes).

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: geonames_readme.txt, "The main 'geoname' table has the following fields": "geonameid         : integer id of record in geonames database"; geonames_readme.txt, "The table 'alternate names'": "geonameid         : geonameId referring to id in table 'geoname', int"
truth.justification: geonameid is the id of a record of the geoname table (the alternate names table refers to it as the id of that table), so one record, hence one value of every other geoname column, belongs to a geonameid.

audit.quote: geonameid : integer id of record in geonames database || geonameid : geonameId referring to id in table 'geoname', int || allCountries.zip : all countries combined in one file, see 'geoname' table for columns
audit.source: geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table || geonames_readme.txt, table 'alternate names' || geonames_readme.txt, Files

truth.clause: geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table: "country code      : ISO-3166 2-letter country code, 2 characters"; geonames_readme.txt, Files: "countryInfo.txt          : country information : iso codes, fips codes, languages, capital ,..."; geonames_countryInfo_header.txt (the '#' comment lines of https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/countryInfo.txt, retrieved 2026-10-28T05:06:38Z), last line (tab-separated): "#ISO ISO3 ISO-Numeric fips Country Capital Area(in sq km) Population Continent tld CurrencyCode CurrencyName Phone Postal Code Format Postal Code Regex Languages geonameid neighbours EquivalentFipsCode"
truth.justification: country code is the ISO-3166 2-letter code, which identifies one country, and countryInfo.txt holds the information of a country under its ISO code (first column), so the code determines the country's ISO3, name, capital, continent and currency; the header's remarks on GB/UK, XK, CS and AN concern which codes exist, not duplicates.

audit.quote: country code : ISO-3166 2-letter country code, 2 characters || XX.zip : features for country with iso code XX || countryInfo.txt : country information : iso codes, fips codes, languages, capital ,... || #ISO ISO3 ISO-Numeric fips Country Capital Area(in sq km) Population Continent tld CurrencyCode CurrencyName
audit.source: geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table || geonames_readme.txt, Files || geonames_readme.txt, Files || geonames_countryInfo_header.txt, last comment line (column header)

truth.clause: geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table: "timezone          : the iana timezone id (see file timeZone.txt) varchar(40)"; geonames_readme.txt, Files: "timeZones.txt            : countryCode, timezoneId, gmt offset on 1st of January, dst offset to gmt on 1st of July (of the current year), rawOffset without DST"
truth.justification: timezone is an IANA time zone id looked up in timeZones.txt, whose offsets are the offsets of that zone, so the id determines them; the readme lists countryCode before timezoneId, so the unpack step must confirm that timezoneId is not repeated under several countries (the offsets of a zone are the same in every row anyway).

audit.quote: timezone : the iana timezone id (see file timeZone.txt) varchar(40) || timeZones.txt : countryCode, timezoneId, gmt offset on 1st of January, dst offset to gmt on 1st of July (of the current year), rawOffset without DST

truth.clause: geonames_readme.txt, AdminCodes: "The corresponding admin feature is found with the same countrycode and adminX codes and the respective feature code ADMx."; geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table: "admin1 code       : fipscode (subject to change to iso code), see exceptions below, see file admin1Codes.txt for display names of this code; varchar(20)"
truth.justification: The readme defines the admin1 feature of a record as the ADM1 record with the same country code and admin1 code (singular: 'the corresponding admin feature'), and refers to a lookup of display names by code, so the pair determines the name of that feature; records with admin1 code '00' ('general features where no specific adm1 code is defined') have no such feature and keep a missing admin1 name.

audit.quote: The corresponding admin feature is found with the same countrycode and adminX codes and the respective feature code ADMx. || admin1 code : fipscode (subject to change to iso code), see exceptions below, see file admin1Codes.txt for display names of this code; varchar(20)

truth.clause: geonames_readme.txt, AdminCodes: "The corresponding admin feature is found with the same countrycode and adminX codes and the respective feature code ADMx."; geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table: "admin2 code       : code for the second administrative division, a county in the US, see file admin2Codes.txt; varchar(80)"; geonames_readme.txt, Files: "admin2Codes.txt          : names for administrative subdivision 'admin2 code' (UTF8), Format : concatenated codes <tab>name <tab> asciiname <tab> geonameId"
truth.justification: The admin2 feature of a record is the ADM2 record with the same country, admin1 and admin2 codes, and admin2Codes.txt lists one name per concatenated country.admin1.admin2 code, so the triple determines the name; records without an admin2 code keep a missing admin2 name.

audit.quote: The corresponding admin feature is found with the same countrycode and adminX codes and the respective feature code ADMx. || admin2 code : code for the second administrative division, a county in the US, see file admin2Codes.txt; varchar(80) || admin2Codes.txt : names for administrative subdivision 'admin2 code' (UTF8), Format : concatenated codes <tab>name <tab> asciiname <tab> geonameId
audit.source: geonames_readme.txt, AdminCodes || geonames_readme.txt, 'geoname' table || geonames_readme.txt, Files
